title: Ang 130–132: more ashtpadis
tomorrow: what is this month of the year asking of you?

segments.voice: Yesterday, the long run: hymns on the stubborn I, and a refrain that gives it away. Hau vari. Today the run comes to its close.

Some people post every workout, every gratitude list, every prayer. Others never mention any of it, not even to their closest friend. Both camps are a little suspicious of the other. So: keep the jewel hidden, or hold it up to the light? On ang 130, as the Majh ashtpadis close, there's a jewel, and one verse that gives each side its best line.
screen: `POST EVERYTHING, OR NOTHING?` → `A JEWEL ON ANG 130.` → `ONE VERSE, TWO SIDES.`

segments.voice: From ang 130 to 132, the last of the Majh ashtpadis are Guru Arjan's. The first opens, in paraphrase: within is the unseen One, who can't be seen; the jewel of the Name is kept hidden. Through the Guru's Word, the unseen is made seen. Sikhs today hold both halves of that, and lean different ways. Here's the private side at its strongest. The Name is a hidden jewel. Simran, remembrance, happens inside, in the breath, where nobody's watching. Practice that's performed can quietly turn into the stubborn I from yesterday: look how devoted I am. Keep it in the heart, and it stays clean. Now the public side at its strongest. The same verse says the Word makes the unseen seen. The Shabad is sung out loud in the sangat, in kirtan, with others. A turban is worn where everyone can see it. A langar feeds whoever walks in. Hide all of it, and nobody else gets to hear. Notice that neither side throws out the other half. The private side still sings in the gurdwara. The public side still sits alone with the Name. The verse keeps the jewel hidden and holds it up, in two lines, and leaves the leaning to you.
screen: `THE JEWEL OF THE NAME, KEPT HIDDEN.` · `THE WORD MAKES THE UNSEEN SEEN.` · `PRIVATE: KEEP IT IN THE HEART.` · `PUBLIC: SING IT WITH OTHERS.` · then, large: `CLOSING HYMNS.`

segments.voice: If you can, read a verse on ang 131 first. Rest one hand over your heart and let it stay there, a private place for a hidden jewel. Breathe slowly behind that hand, with no words and nobody watching. Near the end, lift the hand an inch off your chest, as if showing what's inside, then let it settle back.
Ang 130. The page where the last Majh ashtpadis begin, with the jewel of the Name, hidden and made seen.
Keep it close: closing hymns, a jewel kept hidden and a Word that shows it. Both sides, one verse.
